articles.headline: Sean McVay says Rams to 'evaluate everything' about kicking unit after OT loss
articles.description: After the Rams missed a field goal attempt and had another blocked in Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills, coach Sean McVay said Los Angeles will "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- After the Rams missed a field goal attempt and had another blocked in Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, coach Sean McVay said Los Angeles will "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit.

Rams kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt wide left in the first quarter and had a 48-yard kick blocked in overtime that would have been the winner.

"In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said after the loss. "It cost us the game tonight."

The Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL, according to ESPN Research. The Rams have had 81 missed or blocked kicks under McVay (since 2017, including playoffs), which is third most in the league.

"I felt like I hit it good," Mevis said. "That's all I can tell you. I mean, I hit it good, gave it a chance. I'll have to look."

On the play before the blocked kick, the Rams faced a third-and-5 from the Buffalo 30. Rams running back Kyren Williams was stopped for no gain on the play. After the game, McVay said he wished he had a better play call on third down.

"I'm sick that we came up short, and I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go for it on third down and go to fourth or whatever it was," McVay said. "And that's on me."

McVay said, "It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game."

"We go out there and we give the opportunity for our special teams to kind of go out there and get a field goal," said Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who finished with 17 catches for 138 receiving yards and a touchdown. "We got to be able to execute, and if that's not what we wanted to do, we got to find a way to convert on the critical downs."

The Rams fell to 2-3 despite Matthew Stafford going 40-for-54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns. Los Angeles is in third place in the NFC West behind the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-2 Seattle Seahawks.

articles.headline: Rams' Alaric Jackson punches Bills' Bradley Chubb after MNF
articles.description: On the field after the Los Angeles Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb in a scene captured by ESPN's cameras at SoFi Stadium.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- On the field after the Los Angeles Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb.

In a scene captured by ESPN's cameras, Jackson stood near midfield after the game while exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when it appeared Chubb said something to Jackson. Jackson then walked toward Chubb before punching him in the face with his right hand.

"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game," Chubb told the California Post in Buffalo's locker room. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled."

Jackson was pulled away by Rams tight end Colby Parkinson after the punch.

"Like I said, it was emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb said. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

Chubb was still in full uniform at the time, while Jackson had removed his shoulder pads and jersey before walking up to Chubb.

"Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb said. "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week."

When asked if the punch connected, Chubb responded, "I'm just ready for next week. ... You see, I'm smiling, I'm with my team. ... I'll be ready for next week."

Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson weighed in on social media, writing on X, "So what we gone do about dude hitting Chub!"

Apart from Chubb and Gardner-Johnson's post, neither team addressed the incident.

The Bills will take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, and the Rams host the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.headline: Bills QB Josh Allen earns first overtime win of career vs. Rams on MNF
articles.description: Josh Allen came through with his usual late-game theatrics in leading the Bills to a 37-34 overtime win against the Rams on "Monday Night Football," breaking his careerlong winless streak in OT.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- That's one monkey off Josh Allen's back.

Allen led the Buffalo Bills to a 37-34 overtime win against the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football," breaking his careerlong winless streak in OT. Before Monday's game, Allen was 0-7 in overtime, including three season-ending playoff losses despite him averaging 292 passing yards, 75 rushing yards and a couple of touchdowns per game.

Against the Rams, Allen came through with his usual late-game theatrics. Across the fourth quarter and overtime, Allen was 5-for-5 passing with 121 yards and ran six times for 91 yards and a touchdown. He also completed a 2-point conversion attempt.

But none of that would've mattered if not for edge defender Greg Rousseau blocking the Rams' would-be winning field goal attempt and affording the Bills their chance to end Allen's overtime streak.

"Just didn't feel like I was in a rhythm [early], wasn't taking some of the underneath stuff. Fighting mechanically some stuff right now that I'm working on," Allen said. "But I felt like in that second half I got into a rhythm. Guys made some plays. It's awesome stuff."

Allen acknowledged he crossed his fingers and hoped against hope that a defender would make a play to extend the game in overtime. After that happened, coach Joe Brady didn't take any chances. The Rams had stymied the Bills' passing game, which was already without receivers DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. So the Bills ran four times, twice with running back James Cook and twice by calling Allen's number. On those back-to-back carries, Allen accounted for 19 and 13 yards, pushing his game total to 121, the second-best single-game total of his career.

Ask Allen and Brady and they'll both say they'd prefer to win games without asking Allen to run wild; winning games in which Allen runs 10 times with 12 completions is hardly sustainable. To Brady, Allen is a victim of his own talent sometimes. The mechanical issues Allen can fixate on are often manifestations of an awareness Allen possesses that most others don't.

"I want him to just play," Brady says. "His good is damn good and it's good enough."

In a game in which the Bills committed 13 penalties, gave up 40 completions, turned the ball over twice, including once in overtime, stunk on third downs on offense, struggled on third downs on defense and couldn't get their receivers or tight ends involved in the slightest, having Allen's good was pretty much all the Bills had.

And as evidenced by his big smile caught on camera as Tyler Bass' winning 45-yard kick went through the uprights, Allen's relief after finally getting that overtime win is more than justified.

articles.headline: Lampard: Coventry 'feet on the ground' after Newcastle win
articles.description: Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.
articles.body:
Coventry City boss Frank Lampard is not allowing his side to get carried away after they earned a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle United on Monday.

Jack Rudoni tucked away a sixth-minute penalty after Lukás Hornícek brought down Sidiki Cherif inside the area which gave the hosts a halftime lead.

The Sky Blues made a quick start to the second period as well, and Cherif doubled their lead before Sven Botman's belter halved the deficit with 20 minutes to go -- making for a nervous atmosphere

But Coventry were able to wrap up their first home Premier League win in 25 years courtesy of further efforts from Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni, and make it back-to-back wins for Lampard's newly promoted men.

Lampard, whose side moved up to 14th in the table with the win, was over the moon with his side's performance, but wants them to stay grounded with another "tough" challenge against Tottenham on the horizon.

He said: "We are going to be a relative underdog in pretty much every game, so we have to maximise everything beyond the limit. It's a good feeling for the players.

"They need to keep their feet on the ground because the next one is tough and the one after that is tough. We looked like a team that was hard for teams to come here (and beat) tonight. That's the feeling we haven't had in our first home games this season.

"This gives good confidence, so it's a balance of confidence against over-confidence for us.

"They have to stay humble to that and understand. Every part of the level has gone up."

Coventry failed to score in their first four league matches, but it seems Lampard's side have now broken the shackles after netting five times in their last couple of outings.

Four different players got on the scoresheet, a pleasing sign for Lampard who saw his team finish highest scorers in the Championship last season.

He added: "It's not a nice feeling, looking at the table and seeing zero goals before Forest.

"Your left-back who hardly scores [Jay Dasilva], scores at Forest, it's a lovely story but we need more. It's great and I think it'll be great for lads going forward to feel that confidence.

"Good for all the players that scored and good for the team to feel that we can rely on that."

Another 4-1 defeat for Newcastle means they have now conceded the joint most goals in the league so far alongside Bournemouth and Chelsea.

Boss Matthias Jaissle made it clear that the result was not acceptable, but feels they were better than when they lost by the same scoreline to Leeds a month ago.

He said: "I think it was a tough story throughout the whole match. There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and improve.

"It's not something we can compare with the Leeds match today because I think we were at least better.

"The goals we conceded, it was a different story. We were better after the first 10 minutes, we dominated the game but conceded easy goals, which we need to improve.

articles.headline: Why are Shakhtar playing Champions League games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge?
articles.description: Explaining why Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk will play home Champions League games at Chelsea's stadium.
articles.body:
Shakhtar Donetsk will host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday but the game will be played nearly 1,700 miles from their Ukraine home.

Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's home stadium, will act as Shakhtar's home ground for their European fixtures this season.

ESPN breaks down why that's happening...

Why are Shakhtar playing at Stamford Bridge?

Shakhtar are based in the Ukrainian city of Donetsk.

But they haven't played at their home ground, the Donbas Arena, since 2014. This year, amid security reasons due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, they were seeking a stadium for their four home fixtures in the league phase of the Champions League.

Shakhtar have recently played 'home' European fixtures in Poland, Slovenia and Germany and were linked with using Brentford's stadium this season, but ended up agreeing to play at Stamford Bridge.

FC Shakhtar said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar's matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The 2021 UK census states that approximately 19,000 Ukraine-born people live in London.

How does it affect Chelsea?

Chelsea have no European fixtures this season after finishing 10th in the Premier League last season.

The Blues even cited their "disappointing 2025-26 season and failure to qualify for European football" as part of their reasoning to welcome Shakhtar.

A Chelsea statement said: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

"We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

What matches will Stamford Bridge host?

Shakhtar vs. AEK Athens, Oct. 14

Shakhtar vs. Sporting CP, Nov. 3

Shakhtar vs. Fenerbahce, Nov. 25

Shakhtar vs. Real Madrid, Jan. 27

Chelsea were owned by Roman Abramovich

Chelsea were formerly owned by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.

He was forced to sell the club after 20 years in 2022 under pressure from UK government sanctions after Russia invaded Ukraine.

Where do Shakhtar play home domestic matches?

Shakhtar have largely played their 'home' matches in the Ukrainian league at the Lviv Arena, which is 600 miles from Donetsk, since 2014.

articles.headline: Bills, Josh Allen outlast Rams in overtime on MNF
articles.description: Using a throwback offense with downhill runs and scrambles from their star QB, the Bills escape with the win.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- On a day when it seemed like the Buffalo Bills' defense couldn't make a single play, edge defender Greg Rousseau's special teams prowess and quarterback Josh Allen's legs allowed the Bills to sneak out of "Monday Night Football" with a win.

Allen and the Bills outlasted the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 in overtime using a throwback offense built around downhill runs, screen passes, scrambles and heaves to tight ends absent receivers DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer.

Allen completed only four passes to receivers, but in a game with six lead changes the Bills emerged victorious behind James Cook's 111-yard game and Allen's 121 rushing yards.

To put the Bills' game plan in perspective, the Rams targeted star receiver Puka Nacua more times than Allen threw passes. And the Rams' death-by-a-thousand-cuts offense proved efficient, with QB Matthew Stafford picking apart the depleted and maligned Bills secondary with a barrage of underneath passes.

Injuries to cornerback Christian Benford and safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson made it even tougher to slow the Rams' passing attack late. But Allen and the Bills had possession with seven minutes left in a tie game, and the small-ball offense that benefited coach Joe Brady's bunch all evening came in handy.

The Bills drained 5:35 off the clock and plodded into the red zone for a go-ahead score with 1:39 left. Allen's legs proved most valuable on their final possession of regulation, with scrambles of 15 and 21 yards. Of course, that soon became moot as the Rams went down the field in about 90 seconds thanks to more Stafford mastery and forced overtime.

Both teams made calamitous mistakes in overtime, with Cook fumbling away a would-be scoring drive to start for the Bills and then Rams kicker Harrison Mevis having a would-be game-winning kick blocked by Rousseau to give the Bills another shot. Thirty-two more yards of Allen runs helped the Bills set up Tyler Bass to hit the winning kick.

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Buffalo Bills (4-1)

Trend to watch: James Cook III fumbled two more times, including the overtime fumble that ended a Bills scoring threat. Those were his third and fourth fumbles of the young season, coming off a 2025 campaign in which Cook fumbled six times in the regular season and once more in the playoffs.

What to make of QB performance: Without Moore or Palmer, the Bills' passing attack was muzzled for most of the game. This wasn't much of a surprise. The same sort of thing happened in the second halves against Detroit and New England without Moore. Still, with Allen's receivers consistently unable to pop open downfield, the quarterback incorporated more scrambles into his repertoire than he has since Week 2. All this made Allen seem more human. The fact the Bills played close with this Rams team without a superhuman Allen performance is encouraging, in a sideways type of way.

Stat to know: The Bills converted only two third downs on seven attempts.

articles.headline: Carmelo Anthony thinks Knicks right to halt contract talks to focus on season
articles.description: Former Knicks great Carmelo Anthony said the team is making the right decision in halting contract negotiations with players to focus solely on basketball.
articles.headlineJa: カーメロ・アンソニー、ニックスがシーズンに集中するため契約交渉を中断した判断を支持
articles.descriptionJa: 元ニックスのスター選手であるカーメロ・アンソニーは、バスケットボールに専念するために選手との契約交渉を中断するというチームの決定は正しいと述べた。
articles.body:
STAMFORD, Conn. -- Carmelo Anthony believes the New York Knicks made the right decision in halting contract negotiations with some of their players to focus solely on basketball.

With Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart eligible for extensions but talks going nowhere, the Knicks said last week they were pausing discussions until later in the season and would devote their attention entirely to defending their NBA championship.

Anthony, an All-Star for the Knicks during his Hall of Fame career, said Monday he wasn't alarmed by what he was hearing from a team that should be enjoying happy times.

"I think it's happier times, I just think things just move so fast now that you get a chance to celebrate the championship, then it's business as usual, right? Business has got to go on," Anthony said.

 

"I think it was big for them to stop the conversations, and just, we'll get to that. We'll get to that at the end of the season."

Anthony spoke at NBC Sports studios, where he is preparing for his second season as an analyst for the network's "NBA Showtime" studio show. 

Towns is eligible for a four-year, $276 million deal. He is due to make $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for 2027-28.

He has been disappointed in the progress of talks after being an All-Star in both seasons since coming to New York and told reporters that the Knicks' statement Friday that they were cutting off negotiations "was news to me."

Hart will make $21 million this season and the Knicks have an option for 2027-28 at $22.4 million. He said he wasn't frustrated but had previously noted what it could mean for players at the trade deadline in February if there hadn't been progress on contract talks. 

Anthony was represented by Leon Rose, who is now the Knicks president, when he was traded to New York in 2011. A frequent spectator during the team's title run, he believes the players and management will be able to work things out respectfully.

"But whatever's going to happen is going to happen," Anthony said. "But right now, let the be all be the be all, which is basketball. Let's go defend this championship. And I think both parties understand."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Coventry put four past Newcastle to climb out of relegation zone
articles.description: Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.
articles.body:
Coventry City picked up their first home victory in the Premier League for 25 years with an emphatic 4-1 win over Newcastle United on Monday.

The last time Newcastle played on a Monday night they were hammered 4-1 by Leeds and suffered the same miserable fate in Coventry less than a month later.

Jack Rudoni's sixth-minute penalty gave Frank Lampard's side a dream start and their first Premier League goal in front of their own fans since John Hartson scored in a 1-0 win over Sunderland in April 2001.

It was the first time Coventry fans had seen a Premier League goal at the Coventry Building Society Arena with their last goal in the top flight coming at Highfield Road.

Bobby Thomas' last-man clearance left Matias Fernandez-Pardo waiting for his first goal for the club and that proved to be vital as Sidiki Cherif doubled the hosts lead three minutes into the second period.

Newcastle got themselves back in the contest through a belter from Sven Botman after 70 minutes but Coventry were not to be denied as Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni ensured they moved out of the drop zone with successive wins to draw level on points with Manchester United on a memorable night.

Newcastle started sloppily which set the tone for their disappointing evening, and it led to goalkeeper Lukás Hornícek giving away a penalty in the fourth minute.

The Czech goalkeeper spilled Brandon Thomas-Asante's routine ball and then brought down Cherif before Rudoni calmly sent him the wrong way from 12 yards.

The visitors settled and looked to respond, winger Harvey Barnes looked lively and collected a pass from Joe Willock before firing straight at Carl Rushworth for their first shot on target.

The Sky Blues had a glorious chance to make it two with their first touch inside Newcastle's box since the goal.

Jacob Murphy's cross was cleared by Milan van Ewijk which set Cherif on the counter attack and beyond a high Magpies line but he could only aim straight at Hornicek.

Newcastle should have been on level terms a couple of minutes before the break when Fernandez-Pardo got in behind the Coventry defence from a long clearance, he rounded Rushworth only to see his goalbound effort blocked on the line by the covering Thomas.

Coventry caught Newcastle cold at the start of the second period too as they doubled their advantage.

A long throw into the box was headed out by Malick Thiaw but only into the path of Cherif who arrowed low and hard through several Newcastle bodies and into the bottom right corner.

The Magpies needed something special to get themselves back in the contest and it came when Botman lined one up on the left edge of the area with a bullet too fast for Rushworth to halve the deficit.

The momentum seemingly swung by the way of the visitors but Coventry somehow managed to restore their two-goal lead.

Thomas-Asante dispossessed Joelinton outside his own box and the ball dropped to Simms who saw his effort deflect off Thiaw and in to make it three after 81 minutes

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye move for Fulham youngster King
articles.description: Manchester United are reportedly interested in Fulham teenager Josh King. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United are interested in Fulham teenager Josh King, while Liverpool are looking at Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are watching the situation of Fulham attacker Josh King after being informed that he could be signed for £50 million, according to Football Insider. The 19-year-old is open to the potential of a switch to Old Trafford, but a deal is expected to be more feasible next summer than in January. Multiple clubs in Europe are also looking at King, who has scored two goals in six Premier League matches so far this season.

- Liverpool see Hull City goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis as a potential long-term successor to Alisson Becker, The Sun reports. Tzolakis, 23, has been a standout in the Premier League this season, and Hull are expected to enter talks next month with several suitors keeping tabs on his situation. Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with interest in his signature, with recent reports indicating that his transfer would be valued at £40m.

- Real Madrid are exploring the transfer market for a midfielder as they also prepare to enter contract talks with Jude Bellingham, according to according to Fabrizio Romano. Madrid are keen to find a midfield anchor after missing out on Rodri following his switch to Barcelona in the summer, but they are first prioritizing signing their core players to new deals, with hopes of signing Bellingham, 23, to a two-year extension that will secure his future at the club until the summer of 2031.

- Arsenal are closing in on signing midfielders Declan Rice and Martin Ødegaard to new contracts, while talks are also ongoing with defender Jurriën Timber, TEAMtalk reports. Arsenal are focusing on securing key players to new deals in the coming weeks after making "significant progress," and they are optimistic of confirming all three extensions before January. Rice, 27, and Ødegaard, 27, have both made six Premier League starts this season, while 25-year-old Timber returned from injury last month in the 2-0 league win over Sunderland.

- Liverpool are weighing up their options at right back amid concerns over Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley, with a move for a replacement being considered for the winter transfer window, Football Insider reports. Frimpong, 25, hasn't started a game in the Premier League since August after losing his starting place in the team to Ronald Araújo, while Bradley, 23, is continuing a long return to fitness from a knee injury sustained against Arsenal in January. Barcelona defender Jules Koundé, who has recently been linked with Chelsea, is one of the names on the Reds' shortlist.
